file_checks.result: pass (not re-run: the B3D is deleted by design)
file_checks.evidence: compare_with_reader loads the B3D with nimblephysics.biomechanics.SubjectOnDisk and calls readFrames(trial, 0, n, includeSensorData=False, includeProcessingPasses=True). It finds the dynamics record from nimblephysics' own pass label, which must equal the parquet's pass index (2). It never calls the converter's wire decoder. The values come from nimblephysics attributes pos, vel, acc, tau, groundContactForce, groundContactCenterOfPressure, groundContactTorque, comPos/Vel/Acc and residualWrenchInRootFrame. A field-number or force/CoP/torque mislabel in the converter would therefore show up as a mismatch. Coverage is 134 values per frame: 23 DOF x 4, 3 bodies x 9 contact values, 9 COM values and 6 residuals. That is all 134 signal columns of the 163; the other 29 are identity and metadata. 738 x 134 = 98,892 values, and 3 x 9 x 738 = 19,926 contact values. Equality is exact, and NaN matches only NaN. comparison.json SHA-256 5720c6a0... equals the launcher receipt's output hash, and its fields equal comparison_release.json. Shared with the worker: the column list (conv.columns) and the comparison code itself, written by the same worker and run inside the job. I could not recompute it independently. Metadata columns are outside the comparison; I checked missing_grf_reason separately (item 5).

file_checks.result: pass (low-pass filtering of the forces not checked)
evidence: The converter selects the pass whose type is 'dynamics' in the trial's pass header (order kinematics, lowPassFilter, dynamics; index 2). Every row has source_pass_type 'dynamics' and index 2.

Contact columns come from SubjectOnDiskProcessingPassFrame fields 8, 6 and 7 (ground_contact_force, center_of_pressure, torque). In nimblephysics SubjectOnDisk.proto at c405b056, these fields carry the comment 'These are the original force-plate data in world space, one per ground contact body'. Field 5 (ground_contact_wrench), the root-frame contact copies (14, 18-20) and the joint centres are not written. No column name suggests a predicted, estimated or synthetic force.

Residuals ship as separately named columns: root_residual_0-5 (field 12, root-frame residual wrench) and dynamics_linear/angular_residual (per-frame header arrays). They are labelled residuals, not GRF, and are never added into the contact columns. The proto has no predicted-GRF field.
Plates: the header records 3 force plates for 3 contact bodies (calcn_r, calcn_l, pelvis). Pelvis carries the seat force: 452 N mean while seated and 0 N while standing.

Not checked: the dynamics pass follows a lowPassFilter pass (header: 30 Hz, order 2). These are therefore measured force-plate data, probably filtered, not raw plate samples. Raw readings are not kept by design (D-HIST-04-1 = A). The proto's MissingGRFReason also includes shiftGRF, interpolatedClippedGRF and extendedToNearestPeakForce, which mark frames where AddBiomechanics altered the GRF. None occurs in this pilot.

not_checked_anomalies: Frames 0 and 737, the first and last, have zero force on all three plates but are flagged notMissingGRF, even though the subject is seated (the pelvis plate reads about 450 N in neighbouring frames). A forged or hand-written release record cannot unblock later jobs while the pilot B3D exists, and redirected receipt or transient roots are refused. All 34 plans_r3 specs validate with matching bindings, and the plans/ and plans_r2/ specs are superseded (their bindings no longer match). file_checks.evidence: release_pilot(receipt_dir, out_dir) re-hashes the retained B3D and frames.parquet against the pilot receipt and loads the B3D with nimblephysics.SubjectOnDisk. For every written trial and frame it compares every frames.parquet signal column with the record nimblephysics labels dynamics: exact equality, NaN only matching NaN, and the reader's dynamics index must equal the converter's. It writes comparison.json with counts, hashes, the nimblephysics version and the script and converter hashes, and deletes the B3D only on 0 mismatches with full row coverage. Synthetic run with the real nimblephysics reader: 7 frames, 315 values, 0 mismatches, released in 0.9 s; job 02 then runs. Tampering with frames.parquet after the pilot is refused by the hash check.

pending_comparisons counts a pilot as released only if comparison_release.json records status agree, 0 mismatches, frames_compared equal to the receipt rows (> 0), values > 0, matching B3D and frames.parquet hashes and a nimblephysics version, and the retained B3D no longer exists. A hand-written, field-perfect release record with the B3D present was refused (job 02 blocked). It only passes if the B3D is also deleted by hand. That is deliberate evidence destruction, which no script can prevent, and the launcher and receipts would still show that no 01b job ran.

CLI --run refuses unless --transient-root is DEST, --receipt-dir's parent is DEST/acquisition_receipts and --out is inside DEST. run() always checks pending pilots under fixed_root/acquisition_receipts and leftover B3Ds under fixed_root, whatever paths are passed. Probe: job 02 with redirected receipt and transient roots was refused (B3D under the fixed root).

34 specs (33 acquisition specs plus 01b_release_pilot_fa16_subject_4). guarded_launcher.validate_spec passes for all, and every binding equals the current file (acquisition script 5ff9565c…, converter f8baebfb…). 33 distinct members, none dropped. They sort as 01, 01b, 02. The 01 specs in plans/ and plans_r2/ no longer match their bindings, so the launcher refuses them.

nimblephysics (libtorch) cannot map under the 768 MiB PM-01 cap, so 01b omits address_space_mib (the envelope does not allow a higher cap). In a fresh process, release_pilot on the synthetic B3D peaks at 610 MiB RSS, almost all of it library load. The real pilot B3D is about 10 MB with 738 frames, so a peak of roughly 650 MiB is expected. Startup admission requires 3,584 MiB free on Linux and 2,816 MiB on Windows, the launcher polls a 2,048 MiB floor every 15 s, the timeout is 1,800 s, and the output is one comparison.json. With a bounded 10 MB input and about 2.9 GiB of headroom over the measured peak, runtime polling is sufficient. Not a template: any later nimblephysics job on a large B3D needs its own memory estimate and pilot.

summary: The decoder is right: field numbers, packed encodings and the per-frame layout match the nimblephysics schema and C++. Independent cross-checks with nimblephysics' own C++ reader agree on all 15 real headers and on every frame of the synthetic B3D whose pass order equals the global order. Metadata handling, exclusivity, the one-B3D rule, .rejected handling, the 768 MiB limit, the 33 specs and the deadline arithmetic all hold. Two small fixes are needed before the pilot. (1) nimblephysics labels each per-frame pass record by the global pass list (FramePass::readFromProto: type = header.mPasses[pass]->mType), while the converter uses each trial's own pass-header list. In all 15 real headers the two lists are identical, but the worker's fixture deliberately differs, and there nimblephysics and the converter pick different records. Exclude or refuse such trials so the two readers can never disagree.
